title: Registration and device-enrollment data may reveal household identity
description: During account registration and camera/sensor enrollment, the Home Hub receives identifiers such as name, email, address, account username, device serial numbers, MAC addresses, and room/location labels. If these are exposed in transit, logs, or error messages, an attacker could identify the homeowner and their household.
assumptions: The registration/enrollment flow includes personal account details and unique device identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifying attributes disclosure; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Linkability of multiple enrolled devices to the same homeowner account
description: The Home Hub can associate several cameras and sensors with one account during enrollment. Persistent identifiers and enrollment metadata may allow observers or internal components to link all enrolled devices and actions back to the same household profile.
assumptions: Devices use stable identifiers during enrollment and are bound to a single account.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers.

title: Enrollment metadata may disclose sensitive household context
description: Device names, room assignments, camera placement, and sensor types entered during enrollment can disclose private facts about the home, such as number of rooms, presence of children, security routines, or monitored areas.
assumptions: The homeowner provides descriptive labels or placement information when enrolling devices.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for information disclosure of sensitive personal context.

title: Insufficient proof of consent or action during registration and enrollment
description: If the Home Hub does not keep trustworthy records of what the homeowner agreed to and which devices were enrolled, the homeowner may later be unable to prove or dispute that consent was given for data processing or that a specific device was added.
assumptions: The system relies on enrollment events as evidence of consent or account actions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for repudiation of submitted data/actions; exact node may differ.

title: Unawareness of personal data collected during setup
description: The homeowner may not understand that registration and enrollment collect not only account details but also device identifiers, location labels, and inferred household characteristics, leading to uninformed privacy decisions.
assumptions: Setup UX does not fully explain categories of collected data and downstream uses.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of transparency/awareness.

title: Registration and enrollment may process more personal data than necessary
description: The Home Hub may request excessive personal details or retain enrollment metadata longer than needed, potentially violating data minimization, purpose limitation, or storage limitation obligations.
assumptions: The flow may collect optional profile fields or detailed device metadata beyond what is strictly necessary for setup.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance with privacy principles; exact subtree may vary.

title: Temporary access code can identify a specific guest or visit
description: If the Home Hub receives a code that is unique per guest, booking, or visit window, the code itself can act as an identifier and allow the system or operators to single out which guest is attempting entry.
assumptions: Assumes temporary access codes are unique or mapped to a specific guest, reservation, or time slot.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether the code is treated as a direct or indirect identifier.

title: Guest entry attempts may be linkable across time
description: Repeated submissions of the same temporary access code, or logs of code-entry events tied to the same code, can allow the Home Hub or backend operators to link multiple door-unlock attempts to the same guest or stay.
assumptions: Assumes the Home Hub logs code values or stable pseudonymous references to them across multiple events.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via repeated identifiers/events.

title: Code entry reveals guest presence at home location
description: When a guest enters a temporary access code at the Home Hub, the event reveals that the guest is physically present at the property's front door at a particular time, disclosing location and presence information.
assumptions: Assumes the event is observable, logged, or transmitted beyond the immediate local unlock function.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for presence/location disclosure; exact subtree may differ in a specific LINDDUN Pro catalog.

title: Temporary access code value may be exposed in transit or logs
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest may be disclosed if the Home Hub stores, transmits, or logs the raw code insecurely, enabling others to learn the secret and infer authorized access.
assumptions: Assumes the code is handled beyond volatile local verification or is visible to administrators, logs, or network observers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of sensitive input data; exact node may vary.

title: Guest may be unable to deny a recorded unlock attempt
description: If the Home Hub records the submitted temporary access code together with timestamps, the resulting audit trail can be used to claim that a particular guest attempted or performed entry, reducing the guest's plausible deniability.
assumptions: Assumes logs are retained and associated with a guest identity, reservation, or uniquely assigned code.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation arising from attributable event logging.

title: Guest may be unaware how code-entry data is processed
description: The guest may not understand whether the Home Hub stores the temporary code, logs failed attempts, shares entry events with the host or service provider, or uses the data for security analytics, limiting predictability of processing.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient notice or unclear interface messaging at the point of code entry.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact node naming may differ.

title: Code-entry processing may exceed consent or expected purpose
description: Using the temporary access code or associated entry events for secondary purposes such as guest profiling, behavior analytics, or long-term retention may go beyond what the guest expects when entering a code solely to unlock the door.
assumptions: Assumes secondary use, excessive retention, or insufficient legal basis/notice for processing beyond access control.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance/purpose limitation concerns; exact subtree may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Event log enables linkage of household activity over time
description: A persistent local event log of motion, door, and other sensor events can be correlated across timestamps to link separate observations into detailed household activity patterns, routines, and occupancy profiles.
assumptions: The log stores event timestamps and device or sensor identifiers, and entries persist long enough to be correlated.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for linkability on a data store containing longitudinal event records.

title: Sensor event history can identify residents or visitors
description: Even without explicit names, recurring motion/door/sensor event sequences in the local log may uniquely characterize specific residents, visitors, or a particular household, enabling identification from behavioral patterns.
assumptions: The event history is sufficiently granular and accessible to someone able to analyze patterns.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for identifiability from behavioral/event data rather than direct identifiers.

title: Local event log discloses presence, absence, and routines
description: Stored motion, door, and sensor events reveal when occupants are home, asleep, active, away, or receiving visitors. If accessed by an unauthorized party or overexposed internally, the log discloses sensitive private-life information.
assumptions: The log contents can be read by local administrators, malware, other components, or anyone with device access.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for sensitive information exposure from stored event data.

title: Writing overly detailed events causes unnecessary disclosure
description: The Home Hub may write raw, fine-grained sensor events to the log when coarser summaries would suffice, increasing disclosure of intimate in-home behavior and environmental conditions.
assumptions: The hub controls event granularity and may log more detail than operationally necessary.
uncertainty_note: Same disclosure family applied at the process because the privacy issue originates in what is written to the store.

title: Residents may be unaware that in-home events are persistently logged
description: People in the home, including visitors, may not understand that motion, door, and sensor events are continuously recorded in a local event log, for how long, or for what purposes, undermining predictability and transparency.
assumptions: Notice is limited or absent, especially for non-admin household members and visitors.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for lack of awareness/transparency tied to persistent local logging.

title: Logging may exceed purpose limitation or data minimization expectations
description: Persistently storing detailed sensor events in the local log may be unnecessary for the stated smart-home function, or retained longer than needed, creating risk of non-compliance with privacy requirements such as minimization, retention limits, or purpose limitation.
assumptions: Applicable privacy requirements or user expectations constrain what event data may be logged and how long it may be retained.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for non-compliance related to excessive collection/retention.

title: Event log may not provide trustworthy evidence about who caused an event
description: A local log entry showing a door opened or motion occurred may later be used to infer that a particular resident acted, but the record may not reliably prove who triggered the event, enabling plausible denial or false attribution in household disputes or investigations.
assumptions: Sensor events are later relied upon as evidence of human actions without strong attribution mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central for this flow; included because event logs are often treated as evidence despite weak actor attribution. Node id is approximate.

title: Camera clips contain directly identifying personal data
description: Recorded video clips uploaded by the Home Hub can contain faces, voices, home interiors, visitors, and other directly identifying information about residents and third parties. Sending these clips to cloud storage increases the risk that identities can be inferred or recognized from the content.
assumptions: The uploaded clips contain raw or minimally transformed audio/video footage from home cameras.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for identifiability from data content; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Stored clips can be linked across time to build household activity profiles
description: Cloud video storage can associate multiple uploaded clips from the same Home Hub/account over time, enabling linkage of events into detailed profiles of household routines, occupancy patterns, relationships, and behaviors.
assumptions: Cloud storage retains account, device, or tenant identifiers alongside uploaded clips.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via common identifiers and repeated observations; exact node id may differ in the official tree.

title: Cloud storage can infer sensitive household behaviors from video history
description: By analyzing uploaded clips and their timestamps, the cloud service may determine when residents are home, asleep, away on vacation, receiving visitors, or engaging in sensitive activities. This creates a detectability risk regarding otherwise private states or events.
assumptions: The service can access clip contents and metadata such as timestamps and camera identifiers.
uncertainty_note: I am using detectability here for the ability to observe presence/activities from stored clips; exact node mapping may be approximate.

title: Users or bystanders may be unaware that clips are uploaded to cloud storage
description: Residents, guests, cleaners, delivery personnel, or neighbors captured by the cameras may not know that recordings are being transmitted from the Home Hub to remote cloud storage, reducing transparency about collection and storage locations.
assumptions: The system does not provide clear, timely notice to all affected individuals about cloud upload behavior.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency about data collection and storage; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Uploaded clips may be used for secondary purposes beyond home security
description: Once clips are stored in the cloud, they may be processed for analytics, service improvement, model training, law-enforcement response workflows, or sharing with partners in ways users did not expect or cannot effectively control.
assumptions: Cloud provider terms or backend operations permit or could permit secondary processing beyond primary storage and retrieval.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for secondary use / policy non-compliance from the user's perspective; exact node id may be approximate.

title: Cloud retention and processing of home video may exceed consent or legal basis
description: Storing household video clips in the cloud may violate consent expectations, purpose limitation, data minimization, retention limits, or third-party recording rules, especially for visitors and passersby who did not meaningfully consent.
assumptions: Applicable privacy obligations require explicit notice, lawful basis, minimization, and bounded retention for video data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance with consent, minimization, and retention obligations; exact official node id may vary.

title: Insufficient evidence of upload and access actions can undermine accountability
description: If the cloud storage service does not maintain trustworthy records of when clips were uploaded, accessed, shared, or deleted, it may be difficult for users to prove what happened to their recordings or challenge improper handling.
assumptions: Audit logging, user-visible history, or tamper-evident records may be incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for repudiation/accountability gaps around data handling events; exact node id may differ.

title: Linkability of repeated motion alerts to the same household/device
description: Real-time motion alerts sent from the Home Hub to the backend may carry stable device, household, or account identifiers that allow the backend or anyone with access to backend data to link multiple alerts over time to the same home and build a behavioral profile.
assumptions: The alert payload or transport metadata includes a persistent identifier, account reference, or network-level identifier that remains stable across events.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering for linkability of messages/events may vary.

title: Identifiability of residents from motion alert content and metadata
description: Motion alerts and associated metadata such as device ID, home location, timestamps, and account mapping can make a specific household or resident identifiable to backend operators or attackers who gain access to the backend.
assumptions: The backend can associate the incoming alert with a user account, address, or other identifying subscriber information.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering for identifiability via message metadata may differ.

title: Disclosure of occupancy patterns through stored or observed motion alerts
description: The backend's receipt and possible storage of real-time motion alerts can reveal when people are at home, moving, sleeping, or away, exposing sensitive occupancy and lifestyle patterns if accessed beyond what is necessary.
assumptions: Alerts are logged, retained, monitored, or otherwise accessible at the backend beyond transient routing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for information disclosure from data flow/storage context; numbering may vary.

title: Disclosure of presence at a specific time from real-time alert timing
description: Even if alert payloads are minimized, the timing and frequency of motion alerts received by the backend can disclose highly sensitive information about presence, routines, and daily schedules.
assumptions: Backend systems or observers can access timestamps, traffic patterns, or event frequency information.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an informed estimate for disclosure via metadata/timing side channels.

title: Unawareness of backend processing of motion events
description: Residents may be unaware that each motion event detected by the Home Hub is forwarded to the mobile app backend in real time, including what metadata is included, how long it is retained, and who can access it.
assumptions: User notices or in-product explanations do not clearly describe this real-time transmission and downstream processing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of transparency/awareness; exact numbering may vary.

title: Processing of motion alerts beyond user expectations or legal basis
description: Forwarding real-time motion alerts to the backend may be non-compliant if the processing is not necessary for the stated service, exceeds the declared purpose, lacks valid consent or another legal basis, or retains data longer than permitted.
assumptions: Applicable privacy requirements impose purpose limitation, data minimization, transparency, retention, or lawful-basis obligations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for policy/legal non-compliance; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may differ.

title: Repudiation gaps around transmission and receipt of motion alerts
description: If the system does not provide appropriate records and user-visible evidence of when motion alerts were sent, received, or acted upon, parties may later dispute whether a sensitive alert was transmitted or processed, undermining accountability for privacy-relevant handling.
assumptions: Audit trails, integrity protection, or user-accessible event histories are incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central for this flow than disclosure/linkability; node id is a best-fit estimate.

title: Notification content may disclose occupancy or in-home activity to unintended viewers
description: A motion-detected push notification can reveal that motion occurred at the home, implying presence, absence, routines, or current activity. If the notification text is visible on a lock screen, shared device, wearable, or mirrored display, personal information about the homeowner's household may be exposed to unintended parties.
assumptions: The notification contains explicit or inferable motion-event details and may be displayed outside the app context (e.g., lock screen previews).
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id is approximate; I am using D.1 as a generic information-disclosure/content-exposure node because exact LINDDUN Pro subnode labels can vary.

title: Push delivery metadata can enable linkability of homeowner events across services or devices
description: Sending a motion notification to the homeowner's phone may involve stable device tokens, account identifiers, or correlated timing patterns. These can allow the backend, push provider, or another observer with access to logs to link multiple motion events to the same homeowner or household over time.
assumptions: Push infrastructure uses persistent identifiers or observable metadata such as device token, account id, or consistent endpoint information.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; using L.1 as a generic linkability node.

title: Notification traffic may allow inference of homeowner presence, routines, or lifestyle
description: Even if notification content is minimized, the timing and frequency of motion alerts can allow an observer to infer when occupants are home, asleep, away, receiving visitors, or following recurring routines. This can reveal sensitive behavioral patterns about the homeowner.
assumptions: An attacker or third party can observe notification timing, app activity, network metadata, or device-screen events.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; using I.1 as a generic inference-from-observable-data node.

title: Homeowner may be unaware of what motion-event data is exposed in notifications
description: If the app does not clearly explain notification content, lock-screen behavior, or preview settings, the homeowner may not understand that sensitive motion-event information is exposed outside the app. This reduces user awareness and control over privacy consequences.
assumptions: Notification settings or privacy implications are not clearly communicated during setup or in-app configuration.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; using U.1 as a generic unawareness node.

title: Motion notifications may be sent without valid or sufficiently granular consent/preferences
description: The backend may push motion-detected notifications even when the homeowner has not explicitly consented to this category of alert, has withdrawn consent, or expects more granular controls over what events appear on the device. This can violate user preferences or applicable privacy requirements.
assumptions: Notification preferences, consent state, or per-event privacy settings may be absent, stale, or not enforced consistently by the backend.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; using Nc.1 as a generic non-compliance/consent-and-preference-enforcement node.

title: Analytics dataset may enable linkage with other vendor-held data
description: Even if the backend shares aggregated device-usage analytics, the cloud analytics vendor may combine the dataset with other customer datasets, account metadata, IP ranges, timestamps, app identifiers, or campaign data to link records back to a device cohort, household, or user segment across contexts.
assumptions: The vendor receives sufficient metadata (for example app instance identifiers, tenant identifiers, timestamps, geography, or stable cohort keys) to correlate this flow with other data it already holds.
uncertainty_note: Node id is my best fit for linkability via data correlation; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Aggregated analytics may still permit inference about individuals or small groups
description: Shared usage aggregates can reveal sensitive behavior patterns when cohorts are small or dimensions are too granular. The vendor may infer user habits, presence patterns, feature usage, health-related behavior proxies, or other attributes from segmented analytics.
assumptions: Aggregation may be broken down by fine-grained dimensions such as time, region, device model, feature, or customer segment, creating small-cell statistics.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for inference from released statistics; exact node id may differ in the formal tree.

title: Individuals may be detectable within supposedly aggregated analytics
description: If the analytics include rare events, sparse segments, or near-real-time counts, the vendor may detect that a particular user or device was active, installed the app, used a feature, or belonged to a specific segment, despite the data being described as aggregated.
assumptions: The aggregation threshold may be low, or the vendor may have auxiliary knowledge about a target's app usage window or device characteristics.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as best fit for detectability from aggregate disclosures; exact numbering may vary.

title: Vendor may identify a person or device from aggregate analytics combined with auxiliary data
description: The cloud analytics vendor could re-identify users, devices, or households by combining aggregate usage analytics with its own telemetry, SDK data, advertising identifiers, customer account data, or external datasets. Small cohorts and repeated reports increase this risk.
assumptions: The vendor has access to auxiliary datasets or receives repeated analytics exports over time that allow differencing or reconstruction.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability/re-identification through combination attacks; exact node id may differ.

title: Users may be unaware that backend analytics are shared with an external vendor
description: People may not understand that their app usage contributes to analytics sent from the backend to a third-party cloud analytics vendor, especially when collection occurs server-side rather than directly in the app UI.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-app disclosures do not clearly explain this downstream sharing and its purposes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency; exact node id may vary.

title: Sharing aggregated analytics with the vendor may exceed consent, notice, or purpose limitations
description: The backend may disclose analytics to the vendor without a valid legal basis, outside the scope originally communicated to users, or for secondary analytics purposes incompatible with the original purpose of collection.
assumptions: Applicable privacy requirements or internal policies restrict third-party analytics sharing, require consent/opt-out, or impose purpose limitation and data minimization obligations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for policy/legal non-compliance in third-party sharing; exact node id may vary.

title: Stored video clip may be disclosed to an unauthorized backend context or requester
description: When the backend retrieves a video clip from cloud storage, insufficient authorization checks, overly broad service permissions, or weak binding between the clip and the authenticated homeowner request could expose highly sensitive in-home video to parties other than the intended homeowner.
assumptions: Cloud video storage contains identifiable household video footage and the backend acts on behalf of a user session or account context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id selected for disclosure of data during access/retrieval; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Backend retrieval of a stored clip can reveal homeowner viewing behavior
description: A request by the backend to fetch a specific stored clip can reveal that a particular homeowner is active, interested in a certain time window, or responding to an event. This creates observability of user habits and occupancy-related behavior through access patterns.
assumptions: Storage operators, internal services, or logs can observe which clips are fetched and when.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for identifiability/inference from access patterns rather than direct identity disclosure.

title: Repeated clip retrievals may be linkable to the same household or user account
description: Metadata accompanying retrievals, such as account identifiers, device identifiers, clip IDs, timestamps, or stable backend credentials, can allow observers to link multiple video accesses together and build a profile of a household's routines and incidents over time.
assumptions: Requests or logs contain stable identifiers or quasi-identifiers across sessions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via repeated accesses; exact subtree label may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Video retrieval may exceed the purpose or consent expected by the homeowner
description: If stored clips are retrieved for analytics, troubleshooting, model training, employee review, or other secondary purposes beyond homeowner playback, the flow may violate consent expectations, purpose limitation, or data minimization obligations.
assumptions: The same retrieval path or copied data could be reused beyond immediate playback delivery.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance/consent-purpose issues; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Homeowner may be unaware that stored clips are accessed and processed by backend services
description: The architecture may not provide sufficient transparency that cloud-stored video is fetched, temporarily processed, cached, or logged by backend components before playback. Lack of visibility can undermine user awareness of how their in-home footage is handled.
assumptions: Users do not receive clear notices about backend-side retrieval, caching, or operational logging.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact subtree id may differ.

title: Retrieval path may enable excessive data collection or retention of video content
description: The backend may cache full clips, create duplicate copies, or retain retrieval logs and derived metadata longer than necessary for playback, increasing the amount and persistence of privacy-sensitive household video data.
assumptions: Backend infrastructure may use caching, buffering, observability, or debugging mechanisms that retain content or metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability/discoverability through retained copies and metadata; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping may vary.
